title: SLO Charter & Initiative Runway Planner for Reliability Cohorts
creator: Aisha Park
description: Create a repeatable 'Initiative Runway Planner' and SLO Charter template to coordinate multi-team reliability work across cycles. The goal is to reduce time-to-execution for initiatives that consume or protect error budget, provide guardrails for rollout gating, and map initiative deliverables to OKRs and cycle cadence.
acceptance_criteria: SLO Charter template published in Confluence with fields for owner, SLI definitions, target windows, measurement queries, and rollback gates
Runway Planner spreadsheet that maps initiatives to cycles, estimated error-budget impact, and cross-team dependencies
Two pilot initiatives (Console SLI refactor, Serving runtime batching tweak) onboarded to the planner and tracked for 2 cycles
Dashboard widgets that surface initiative-level SLI trends and projected error-budget burn for the next 7 days
Runbook includes automated gating criteria and an owner contact matrix for emergency rollback
decisions: Adopt cohort-based runway: group initiatives by shared SLO targets and customer surface to limit blast radius
Use 7d/28d windows as canonical SLI windows for initiative impact modeling (matches existing telemetry)
Gating threshold set at 30% of weekly error-budget consumption for automated rollback alerting; >50% triggers canary throttle
Initiatives must include a 'rollback PR' or toggle before reaching production rollout stage
tradeoffs: Tighter SLO enforcement reduces risk but may slow feature velocity (we accept controlled slower rollout for high-customer-impact services)
Automation for gating requires more upfront instrumentation effort from teams, but reduces manual on-call load during rollouts
7d windows are more sensitive and actionable but noisier; 28d windows provide stability but delay detection
